title: Two-track release notes runbook with translation + embargo handling
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a repeatable two-track release notes runbook that separates an internal operational digest from a customer-facing changelog. The runbook must include: (1) an automated draft generator that pulls PR titles/descr and linking metadata, (2) a lightweight legal/redaction checklist, (3) an embargo & rollback decision matrix, and (4) a translation pipeline for high-traffic markets (EN, FR, DE, JP) that balances speed and editorial review. Purpose: reduce churn in draft creation, shorten review cycles, and reduce customer confusion during staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc in Confluence with versioned template and checklist
Automated draft generator emits a first-pass changelog JSON for each release (sample output linked)
Signoff flow defined and automated: PM -> Legal -> Comms -> Design -> Ops, with explicit SLA for each step
Embargo matrix defined with clear triggers for moving from embargoed to public and rollback steps documented
Translation pipeline defined with fallback: machine translation + human review for top markets; timelines included
At least one canary release uses the new runbook end-to-end and we capture time-to-publish metrics

2026-03-08 Rafael Gomez: Updated PoC generator to attach GitHub PR links and issue keys. Early trade-off: if we include full PR body we risk exposing internal discussion; decided to only surface PR summary with link to GH for authorized viewers.
2026-03-09 Ops (Priya Nair): Requested explicit rollback playbook entries with runbook cross-links to incident procedures. Noted dependency on the rollout automation for Dedicated capacity changes.

next_steps: 2026-03-15: Dry run with a canary release (platform-canary) to exercise end-to-end runbook
Add contract-team redaction trigger to generator (ENG-23145) and run tests
Create automated Slack notification to #release-ops with internal digest and link to customer publish preview
Build lightweight UI for 'signoff' that records timestamped approvals (prototype in Notion)
Measure and record time-to-publish for dry run; target median <= 24 hours from draft generation to publish
decisions: Keep internal digest separate from customer changelog to avoid leaking operational details to customers.
Automated draft will only include PR summary and link; full PR body is not surfaced in customer copy.
Use machine translation (MT) + human review for EN->FR/DE/JP; fall back to MT-only for low-impact releases to meet SLAs.
Embargo policy: default 48-hour embargo for security-sensitive changes; emergency exceptions require executive OK and Ops-led rollback steps.
Redaction: introduce a two-flag system in PR labels: 'changelog-public' and 'changelog-private' to guide generator inclusion.
